title: Federal Judge in Los Angeles Issues Tentative Injunction Blocking ICE Warrantless Arrests Without Flight-Risk Assessment
excerpt: U.S. District Judge Maame Ewusi-Mensah Frimpong in Los Angeles issued a tentative ruling to grant a preliminary injunction requiring ICE agents to document individualized flight-risk assessments before making warrantless arrests. The ruling would make her the fifth federal judge to block the administration's warrantless arrest practices, following courts in Oregon, Colorado, and Washington D.C.
content:
On August 13, 2026, U.S. District Judge Maame Ewusi-Mensah Frimpong indicated she would issue a preliminary injunction barring ICE agents in the Los Angeles region from making warrantless arrests without an individualized assessment of whether the person posed a flight risk.

The tentative ruling would make Frimpong the fifth federal judge to block the administration's warrantless arrest practices, following courts in Oregon, Colorado, and Washington D.C. Two courts had also already found that ICE agents continued warrantless arrests even after being ordered to stop.

  • Attorneys for immigrants swept up in LA raids reviewed 113 arrest reports and found that nearly 80% contained no genuine assessment of flight risk, relying instead on boilerplate language.
  • A Border Patrol supervisor testified in deposition that a person's "self-admission of alienage" was sufficient to justify a warrantless arrest—a standard attorneys said was inconsistent with federal law in place since 1946.
  • The ruling is distinct from the court's 2025 order barring agents from stopping people based on race, Spanish-speaking, or clothing; this new order addresses what information agents must collect before arresting someone without a warrant.
  • Attorneys released hundreds of new exhibits including body camera footage, text messages, and official ICE headquarters orders as part of the motion.
